question: Coverage of an explicit aggregate-block implementation of the manuscript's one-window joint fit and percentile interval
block_sampling: For each target segment and arm, sample source starts uniformly with replacement from the same segment; concatenate contiguous source runs, truncating the last run to the target segment length.
risk_set_seam: Fix each arm's original enrollment count. At each resampled target bin apply the source bin's deaths/at-risk fraction to the reconstructed current risk set, round to the nearest integer, cap at the current risk set, and decrement the risk set. This enforces N(t)=N(0)-sum of earlier deaths exactly.
fit: Use the manuscript's joint k/theta least-squares objective in weeks 6-40, exact cumulative gamma inversion, and normalization by week-5 cumulative ratio. In this single-window no-wave setting, Step 4 has the same objective as Step 1 and no offset to align.
bootstrap_fit_starts: Warm start theta at the original dataset's fitted theta; confirm against the four-start fit on a prespecified subset of draws and fall back to all starts on failure.
interval: Unadjusted 2.5th and 97.5th empirical percentiles of bootstrap KCOR at week 52
acceptance: Report all datasets, optimizer success, finite intervals, boundary fits, and any diagnostic proxy separately. The manuscript does not give numeric thresholds for its full diagnostic pass rule; do not claim calibrated conditional-on-diagnostic-pass coverage.
decision: A material coverage failure in the main version supports a failure of this version only. Agreement across prespecified block lengths strengthens the inference. Near-nominal coverage of a version does not validate the uniquely intended paper method or its missing diagnostic gate.
